title: CSV to HTML Table Converter – Free, Private | OpenAnyDoc
description: Convert CSV to an HTML table with thead and tbody: a full UTF-8 page that opens in any browser, or just the table to paste into your site. No upload.
heading: CSV to HTML Table
subtitle: Drop a CSV and get an HTML table at once: a full page or just the table, ready to copy or download.
intro: Publish a spreadsheet on a web page, in an email template or in a CMS without hand-writing table tags. Choose, drop or paste a CSV or TSV file and the HTML appears at once: a <table> with the header row in <thead> and the data in <tbody>. Pick Full page for a complete UTF-8 HTML file that opens in any browser, with each cell set to dir="auto" so Arabic reads right to left, or Table only to paste the <table> into a page you already have. Text is escaped, so <, > and & in your data show as written. The file is read in your browser and never uploaded.

features.title: Private
features.text: Your CSV is turned into HTML by your own browser and never sent to a server.

features.title: Full page or table only
features.text: Download a standalone page that opens in any browser, or copy just the <table> for your own site or template.

features.title: Works offline
features.text: Once this page has loaded, it keeps working without an internet connection.

stepsTitle: How it works: convert CSV to an HTML table

steps.title: Add your CSV
steps.text: Choose or drop a .csv or .tsv file, paste CSV text into the box, or try a sample.

steps.title: Choose the output
steps.text: Full page writes a complete HTML file; Table only writes just the <table> element.

steps.title: Copy or download
steps.text: Copy the HTML to your clipboard or download it as a .html file with the CSV's name.

handlesTitle: What the CSV to HTML converter handles
handles: Files: .csv and .tsv, or CSV text you paste; comma, semicolon, tab and pipe delimiters.
Encodings: UTF-8, UTF-16 (when the file starts with a byte order mark), Windows-1256 Arabic and Windows-1252 Western European text, written as a UTF-8 page.
Structure: <table> with the header row in <thead> and every other row in <tbody>.
Arabic and mixed text: in a full page each cell has dir="auto", so each cell reads in its own direction.
Escaping: <, > and & in cells are written as entities, so data is never read as markup.
limits: The table carries no styling; add your own CSS for borders, colours and widths.
The preview shows the first 5,000 lines; Copy and Download always take the whole HTML.
faqTitle: CSV to HTML: questions and answers

faq.question: Is my file uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Your browser reads the CSV and writes the HTML on your device. Pasted text stays in this tab and is never sent anywhere.

faq.question: What is the difference between Full page and Table only?
faq.answer:
Full page writes a complete HTML file with a UTF-8 declaration that you can open in a browser on its own. Table only writes just the …
to paste into an existing page, a CMS or an email template.

faq.question: Will Arabic text display correctly?
faq.answer: Yes. The page is UTF-8 and, in Full page, each cell has dir="auto", so Arabic cells read right to left while English and number cells stay left to right.

faq.question: Is it safe if my data contains < or & characters?
faq.answer: Yes. Those characters are escaped, so a cell such as 5 & 6 shows as that text instead of being read as HTML.

faq.question: Why does the table look plain?
faq.answer: The converter writes clean table markup with no styling, so it fits your site's look. Add CSS for borders, padding and colours.

faq.question: Can I view the CSV as a table without converting?
faq.answer: Yes. The CSV viewer opens the file as a sortable, searchable table in your browser.

faq.question: How do I convert a CSV file to an HTML table?
faq.answer: Open or paste the CSV, choose Full page or Table only, then copy the HTML or download it as a .html file. OpenAnyDoc writes the table in your browser, so the data is never uploaded.
